name: Chaetopappa

project_scope.source_pool: Live Master Plant Pool; all three already canonical; range statuses unchanged

look_here_first: Check mature stem leaves first: densely overlapping narrow leathery grooved leaves point to C. ericoides. If leaves are flat and uncrowded, expose the base: a taprooted annual is C. bellidifolia; a rhizomatous perennial with broad proximal leaves is C. effusa. Confirm with mature cypsela pappus, not ray color.

shared_traits: Small annual or perennial composites with alternate simple leaves and solitary terminal radiate heads.
Head has ray and disk florets and an involucre of several phyllary series; ripe cypsela/pappus provides critical characters.
All three may have pale rays and yellow disks; flower color and small size are shared, not separating.
priority: Leaf overlap, texture and adaxial grooves
Mature pappus: bristles versus minute ring
Proximal cauline leaf width and base
study_strategy.warning: Detached flowering heads and immature fruits rarely establish a safe species ID. C. bellidifolia and C. effusa BOTH have tiny ringlike pappi.

species_comparison_matrix.ericoides: One series of usually 24–26 (sometimes 20–30) white barbellate bristles

species_comparison_matrix.effusa: Small solitary radiate head; pale rays
species_comparison_matrix.ericoides: Small solitary radiate head; white/pink rays

quick_key.if: Densely overlapping leathery grooved leaves and one row of ~24–26 mature pappus bristles
Flat non-overlapping leaves, distinct annual taproot and tiny pappus ring
Flat non-overlapping leaves, rhizomes, proximal blades 6–12 mm wide with truncate/subcordate bases and tiny pappus crown
Only an immature head or broken stem is available
quick_key.then: Chaetopappa sp. — seek rootstock and ripe cypsela

comparison_cards.title: C. ericoides versus C. bellidifolia and C. effusa
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare equal-length leafy stems and ripe cypselae.

field_matrix.ericoides: Tiny, densely overlapping, leathery and grooved

comparison_cards.caution: Count only mature fruit; drought may change leaf crowding.

comparison_cards.title: C. bellidifolia versus C. effusa
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Expose the intact rootstock; pappus rings overlap.
comparison_cards.caution: Both have tiny ringlike pappi, so fruit alone cannot split this pair.

overlap_and_cautions: White/pink rays, yellow disk and small heads overlap.
A broken root does not prove annuality; seek an intact base.
C. parryi resembles rhizomatous effusa but has 2–5 mm proximal leaves and a larger 0.3–0.8 mm hyaline pappus crown.
C. hersheyi resembles leafy ericoides but has a two-series pappus with about five long inner bristles and outer scales.
Small-rayed Erigeron spp. are plausible look-alikes; inspect involucre and mature fruit with an appropriate key, not color.

local_lookalike_routing.check: Whole head, phyllaries, ripe pappus and plant base; no universal visual shortcut.
Proximal leaf width 2–5 mm; pappus crown 0.3–0.8 mm.
Two-series pappus: outer scales and ~5 inner bristles.
